summary.short: German Digital Services Act implementation statute (DDG). Implements Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) for digital intermediary services: designates competent authorities, creates a Digital Services Coordinator, sets liability, blocking and information rules, enforcement powers and fines. From the table of contents only; operative text not in the fetched document.
summary.long: The DDG is a German statute that implements Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) for digital services. Part 1 sets general rules: scope and definitions, the European seat of providers, a country-of-origin principle and freedom of admission. Part 2 sets general information duties and special duties for commercial communications. Part 3 covers users' infringements: limited liability of providers and a claim to blocking. Part 4 covers audiovisual media service and video-sharing platform providers, including provider lists, information requests and contractual use bans. Part 5 designates competent authorities and sets up a Digital Services Coordinator with a central complaints office and advisory board; it also covers reporting suspected offences to the Federal Criminal Police Office. Part 6 assigns further authorities under Regulations (EU) 2019/1150, 2024/1028 and 2018/302 and a liaison point under Directive 2000/31/EC. Part 7 sets investigation, information, search and seizure powers, enforcement, public information, Federal Network Agency powers, legal remedies and procedure. Part 8 contains fine provisions. Part 9 contains transitional and final provisions and an evaluation clause. Only the table of contents was fetched: provision texts, entry-into-force dates and penalty amounts are not stated in this document.
